items.name: En route centers (ARTCC buildings)
items.after_2028: Still 60+ (one new consolidated ARTCC funded; five more in the $50.1B request)
items.note: FAA COO, 2024: designed for 50 years, now 60 to 70 on average. Last built 1969 (dot_501).

items.name: Copper telecom lines
items.after_2028: Replaced by fiber, wireless, LEO satellite
items.note: Date from the 1960s; no longer supported by providers.

items.name: Surveillance radars
items.note: 'Most of our radars date back to the 1980s' (DOT). GAO: past their 20-year planned life.

items.name: Combined TRACON/towers
items.after_2028: Unchanged by phase 1; up to 140 towers in the $50.1B request
items.note: 132 combined facilities averaging about 35 years. Design life per OIG: 25 to 30 (oig2008). Undated testimony; treat as approximate.

items.name: Voice switches
items.note: Oldest technology deployed in the 1990s; most past end-of-life.

items.name: ERAM en route automation
items.after_2028: Upgrades only; replacement is in the unfunded software phase

facts.text: 37% of FAA's 138 ATC systems were rated unsustainable and 39% potentially unsustainable (2024)
Of the most critical at-risk systems GAO listed, two were over 40 years old and seven over 30
Flight-delay minutes from equipment issues in 2025 were about 300% above the 2010 to 2024 average
Many older voice radios have been out of production since 2015 or earlier
